messages:
elena: heads up — AcmeCorp is seeing a spike of embed rejections from the indexer starting ~10:00 UTC. Customer says recent model swap might've changed dims. They see a bunch of 400s from /v1/embeddings and then indexer rejects with `dim_mismatch`. Also customers reported higher latency and a couple billing complaints where they were charged for failed batches.

samir: thx. do we have a sample request/id from them? can you paste the request_id and model name? also any auth errors?

elena: request_id=rp_8f3f2a9c, model=public-embed-xl-v2 (they were migrated yesterday). No auth errors — tokens ok. Example payload: `{"input": ["doc1","doc2"], "model": "public-embed-xl-v2"}`. Response headers show `x-embed-dim: 1024` for some items and `x-embed-dim: 1536` for others in the same batch.

ingest-sre-bot: alert: indexer rejected 824 vectors (code: DIM_MISMATCH) in pipeline ingest-v2 between 1719502400-1719502600. Backpressure engaged at queue ingest-default-queue.

eng-ingest: hitting this now — looks like mixed-dim vectors entering the same batch. Our indexer enforces uniform dims per request. Two quick possibilities: (1) model variant returned different dims for truncated inputs (unlikely) or (2) batching combined items produced by different model versions / model family.

samir: are we certain the embed service returned mixed dims in a single HTTP response, or were multiple requests batched downstream? can we get raw responses?

elena: attached a minimized raw response from Acme (pasted below). note same HTTP response with an array of embeddings where lengths differ.

--- raw response (sanitized) ---
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"data": [
  {"embedding": [0.12, 0.34, ...], "meta": {"_dim": 1024}},
  {"embedding": [0.22, 0.11, ... , 0.07], "meta": {"_dim": 1536}}
]}

maya: this is interesting — during yesterday's rollout we had two model binary variants on the serving fleet (quantized vs float). autoscaler may have routed different requests to different backends and a downstream collector aggregated them into one batch. that would produce mixed dims.

ada: confirmed in tracing: trace=tr_7c9d; request group aggregated two upstream embed responses before enqueueing to indexer. collector process assumes homogenous dims and didn't validate. filing bug in collector to reject mixed-dim merges.

eng-ingest: immediate mitigation options — (A) pin the customer to previous model version (public-embed-xl-v1) to stop new mixed responses; (B) update the collector to validate dim per-item and split batches with mixed dims so indexer gets uniform batches; (C) temporarily relax indexer to accept dim as metadata (not ideal).

samir: customer-facing plan? they want a timeline and want refunds for failed charges.

elena: proposed reply to Acme: explain root cause (model rollout + collector merged responses), offer to pin them back to v1 and run a focused backfill for rejected vectors, and propose a credit for the failed batches. asking eng for ETA on collector fix and safe backfill instructions.

eng-ingest: ETA: patch to collector to validate+split is ~4h for an emergency release (hotfix + canary). Backfill approach: 1) pin model for live traffic; 2) run backfill job that re-ingests rejected payloads from dlq with per-item dim validation; 3) convert rejected items into two separate backfills by target-dim and index into the proper vector collection or create a migration that normalizes dims (we should avoid auto-truncation). We'll need a small migration job to tag vectors with model_version and dim.

maya: also found secondary issue — billing pipeline recorded tokens consumed per upstream response but didn't tie success/failure to billing cutoff, so failed batches got charged. billing team should zero out charges for requests where indexer returned permanent rejects within 24h. tagging finance for manual credits. :exclamation:

ada: reproducible repro steps for SRE/eng:
1) deploy two embed backends with different dims on canary route.
2) send 10 requests with mixed routing (script attached) to collector endpoint that merges responses.
3) observe collector create a single batch with mixed-dim items and indexer rejecting some.

script snippet:
```
for i in 1..10; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/integrations/collector -d '{"inputs": ["a","b","c"], "model_hint": "random-route"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
done
```

eng-ingest: I'll push the collector hotfix to `hotfix/collector-dim-guard` and do a canary at 5% in eu-west-1. Once verified we'll ramp and run the backfill. Backfill ops will require a maintenance window (no live writes to the same index) — estimate 6-8h for Acme's dataset (~40M vectors) if we do safe re-ingest with dedupe.

samir: for the customer reply: can we do pin+credit within next 2h, and run a coordinated backfill in next 24-48h?

eng-ingest: pin to v1 — trivial, I can do it now (will update routing table). Credit requests — tagging finance and ops. Hotfix deploy in ~4h, backfill scheduling after canary success.

elena: I'll send Acme the mitigation + timeline. please paste final routing pin and credit ticket once created. thanks all. :pray:
